title: Understanding Model Risk
text: Model risk is influenced by three main components: model bias, model variance, and observational variance. Consider how each of these might be affected by inaccurate survey responses.

title: Impact of Lying on Observational Variance
text: Observational variance refers to the variability in the data that cannot be explained by the model. If survey responses are inaccurate, how might this affect the observational variance?

hintAnswer: The model risk increases because the observational variance increases.
title: Analyzing the Effect on Model Risk
text: Given that the survey responses are inaccurate, which component of model risk is most likely to increase?
choices: The model risk increases because the model bias increases.
The model risk increases because the model variance increases.
The model risk increases because the observational variance increases.
The model risk decreases because the model bias decreases.
The model risk decreases because the model variance decreases.
The model risk decreases because the observational variance decreases.
The model risk stays the same because the lying consumers have no effect on model bias, model variance, or observational variance.
